papers.title: Dynamic Decomposition of Spatiotemporal Neural Signals
papers.abstract: Neural signals are characterized by rich temporal and spatiotemporal dynamics that reflect the organization of cortical networks. Theoretical research has shown how neural networks can operate at different dynamic ranges that correspond to specific types of information processing. Here we present a data analysis framework that uses a linearized model of these dynamic states in order to decompose the measured neural signal into a series of components that capture both rhythmic and non-rhythmic neural activity. The method is based on stochastic differential equations and Gaussian process regression. Through computer simulations and analysis of magnetoencephalographic data, we demonstrate the efficacy of the method in identifying meaningful modulations of oscillatory signals corrupted by structured temporal and spatiotemporal noise. These results suggest that the method is particularly suitable for the analysis and interpretation of complex temporal and spatiotemporal neural signals.

summary_zh.motivation: 提出分解神经信号中节律与非节律成分的方法
summary_zh.method: 基于随机微分方程和高斯过程回归
summary_zh.result: 成功从模拟和MEG数据中识别有意义调制

summary_en.motivation: To decompose neural signals into rhythmic and non-rhythmic components capturing cortical dynamics
summary_en.method: Using stochastic differential equations and Gaussian process regression to model dynamics
summary_en.result: The method effectively identifies modulations of oscillatory signals in both simulations and MEG data
summary_en.validation: Validated through computer simulations and magnetoencephalographic data

papers.title: Microstructure, defects and mechanical behavior of beta-type titanium porous structures manufactured by electron beam melting and selective laser melting

corresponding_authors.name: Shujing Li
corresponding_authors.affiliation: Shenyang National Laboratory for Materials Science, Institute of Metal Research, Chinese Academy of Sciences, 72 Wenhua Road, Shenyang 110016, China

corresponding_authors.name: Lai‐Chang Zhang
corresponding_authors.affiliation: School of Engineering, Edith Cowan University, 270 Joondalup Drive, Joondalup, Perth, WA 6027, Australia

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文直接研究了用于生物医用植入体的β钛多孔结构在EBM和SLM工艺下的力学行为，与用户关注的LPBF制造、刚度匹配和应力遮挡高度相关。
llm.why_not_core: No fatigue testing or surface roughness/osseointegration analysis is reported.

summary_zh.motivation: 研究β钛多孔结构在两种增材制造工艺下的力学行为
summary_zh.method: 对比电子束熔融与选区激光熔化制备的多孔钛样品
summary_zh.result: 揭示了工艺-缺陷-力学性能的关系
summary_zh.validation: 通过压缩试验验证力学性能

summary_en.motivation: To compare microstructure and mechanical behavior of beta-type titanium porous structures fabricated by EBM and SLM for biomedical applications.
summary_en.method: Beta-Ti porous structures were manufactured by both processes and characterized for defects and mechanical properties.
summary_en.result: Process-induced defects significantly influence mechanical behavior; SLM yields higher strength but more defects than EBM.
summary_en.validation: Mechanical compression testing was performed to evaluate stiffness and strength.

papers.title: Strength analysis and modeling of cellular lattice structures manufactured using selective laser melting for tooling applications
papers.first_author_affiliation: Technical University of Denmark, Department of Mechanical Engineering, Lyngby, Denmark

corresponding_authors.name: Rasoul Mahshid
corresponding_authors.affiliation: Technical University of Denmark, Department of Mechanical Engineering, Lyngby, Denmark

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文专注于工具应用，未涉及生物医学植入物的应力遮挡或骨整合问题。
llm.why_not_core: The paper addresses lattice structures for tooling, not biomedical implants, and lacks any mention of stress shielding, stiffness matching, fatigue, or osseointegration.

summary_zh.motivation: 为工具应用开发高强度多孔晶格结构。
summary_zh.method: 采用选择性激光熔化制造晶格结构并进行力学建模。
summary_zh.result: 建立了强度预测模型，验证了制造工艺的可行性。
summary_zh.validation: 通过力学实验验证模型精度。

summary_en.motivation: To develop high-strength cellular lattice structures for tooling applications using selective laser melting.
summary_en.method: Lattice structures were fabricated via selective laser melting and modeled for strength analysis.
summary_en.result: A predictive model for lattice strength was established and validated experimentally.
summary_en.validation: Experimental mechanical testing confirmed the model predictions.
